CHAPTER ONE
The morning began quietly. Mira opened the window and listened to the street below. A bicycle bell crossed the square. Somewhere nearby, a baker lifted the shutters. She packed a notebook, a blue pen, and the letter she had avoided reading. The train would leave before noon. For the first time in months, she felt ready to follow it.
CHAPTER TWO
The carriage smelled of rain and old wool. Fields moved past the glass in long green ribbons. Mira read the first line of the letter, paused, and started again. The words were kinder than memory had made them. By the next station, she had reached the final page. She folded it carefully and watched the hills draw closer.
EPILOGUE
At dusk, the house appeared beyond the trees. One lamp waited in the upstairs window. Mira crossed the garden without hurrying. When the door opened, neither of them needed to explain the years between them. The long journey ended with a simple welcome home.
